messages:
alicia: Quick follow-up from last night's postmortem (link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-21-latency). Main points: recurring p99 spikes ~03:00 UTC, KV cache cold miss surge, and batching backpressure on a few GPU nodes. I listed proposed action items below — need owners + realistic timelines.

alicia: ACTIONS: 
• A1: Add fine-grained KV cache metrics & retention curve (owner?, due)
• A2: Add per-model batch-size histogram and hot-node alert (owner?, due)
• A3: Short-term SLO tweak + SLA impact assessment (who owns the change request?)
• A4: Canary rollback/runbook update + runbook drill (owner?, due)

ben: I'll take A1 (KV metrics). Planning to add latency by key/namespace, and a 7/30d retention chart. Targeting 2026-04-02 for initial dashboard.

chao: I can pick A2 (batch histograms). I'll add a Prometheus export + Grafana panel and a hot-node alert rule that fires at sustained tail batch_size>80 for 5m. ETA 2026-03-30.

marta: For A3 (SLO tweak) — we should be careful. Current p99 target is `120ms` for host inference; we burned 35% error budget last week. Proposal: temporarily relax p99 to `150ms` for 2 weeks while infra mitigations land, and add an annotation in the SLA tracker. I can draft the change request and impact note. Who signs off on SLA changes?

alicia: @marta please draft the change request. We'll need legal + ops signoff for any SLA wording change; ops (me) will route it. Also add a regression test to Redwood Optimize evals for the new threshold.

ben: small note on A1: adding prefix/KV TTL histogram will help identify cold-start churn. I'll include a small sampling agent to avoid cardinality blowup.

chao: For alerts: propose an aggregate error-budget burn alert (72% burn over 7d) + a separate pattern alert for recurring 03:00 UTC spike (use bootstrap window). If both fire, escalate to oncall + SRE pager.

marta: Agree. For the SLO temporary change, suggest these steps: 1) Draft CR and notify customers (if relevant); 2) Adjust monitoring dashboards with clear banner; 3) Create a post-change verification runbook. I'll draft by EOD 2026-03-24.

incident-bot: Ticket created: REDW-4127 — "Postmortem follow-ups: KV metrics, batch histograms, SLO assessment, canary runbook" assigned to triage. https://redwood.internal/tickets/REDW-4127

ben: REDW-4127 updated: A1 assignee ben, 2026-04-02. Linking PR template: ```scripts/telemetry/add_kv_metrics.md```

chao: REDW-4127 updated: A2 assignee chao, 2026-03-30. Grafana panel name: `SRE / Batch / Per-model batch_size histogram`

alicia: For A4 (runbook + drill) I'll coordinate. Suggest a drill window next Tue 03:00-04:00 UTC where we validate canary rollback and runbook steps with the oncall. Tentative owner: alicia, due 2026-03-29.

marta: Quick ask about customer-facing SLA: if we relax p99 to 150ms for 2 weeks, ops should log an internal incident note and we should push a short advisory to impacted customers no later than the change window. I'll draft advisory text and share for review.

ben: thumbs up. Also adding a KV cache warmup during scale-up (pre-warm policy) as a mitigation; will include as a follow-on task in REDW-4127.

chao: One more pattern callout: the 03:00 spikes correlate with nightly model checkpoint sync on a subset of hosts. I'm opening a separate infra ticket to stagger checkpointing by shard. If we can move that off the p99-critical nodes the spikes drop by ~40% in the replay.

alicia: Awesome. Summary now: A1 ben (2026-04-02), A2 chao (2026-03-30), A3 marta draft + ops signoff (draft 2026-03-24), A4 alicia drill (2026-03-29). Next check-in in #eng-sre on 2026-03-25 16:00 UTC to verify dashboard changes and CR progress. If anything slips, ping @alicia or update REDW-4127. :eyes: 

ben: got it.

marta: will post draft advisory in this thread when ready.

chao: I'll add the Grafana link and sample query in REDW-4127 shortly.

alicia: Thanks everyone — close the loop in REDW-4127 and I'll prepare the ops signoff packet.
